themes.0.1.0: Ready for the benchmarks being written now
themes.0.2.0: Passing takes more than retrieving everything

items.title: "None on record" only where it's true
items.blurb: An attempt that says "none on record" for a question whose answer is on record fails, and the baseline stops saying it there.

acceptance.criterion: An attempt that says "none on record" for a question whose answer is on record fails
The baseline says "none on record" only for wine's one question whose answer it is
The baseline still passes every question in wine's benchmark

items.title: Grade a graph published as several files
items.blurb: baseline --graph can repeat, so a schema that publishes one Turtle file per dataset no longer has to be concatenated first.

acceptance.criterion: --graph may be given more than once, and every file loads into one store
A graph split across files retrieves the same as the whole

items.title: "None on record" questions about one record
items.blurb: Some of these questions name one record and a kind of record: "Is there a purchase of cotija?" The baseline answers "none on record" when no record of that kind is linked to the one named.

acceptance.criterion: The baseline says "none on record" when the question names one record and a class, and no instance of the class is adjacent to it
It does not when an instance of the class is adjacent
The baseline still never reads the key

items.title: A retrieval budget
items.blurb: Anchors must be reached within a cap on how many records are retrieved, so retrieving the whole graph stops passing. The cap may belong in the benchmark rather than the grader.

acceptance.criterion: An attempt that retrieves more than the budget fails anchors-reached

items.title: Citation precision
items.blurb: Citing everything that was retrieved stops passing attribution.

acceptance.criterion: Attribution fails when the share of citations the key expects is under the floor

items.title: Read the answer key from its source
items.blurb: The key is read from the benchmark's YAML, through panschema's model of the cqa schema, instead of from its Turtle rendering.

acceptance.criterion: The YAML and Turtle readers give the same benchmark for wine

items.title: Alternative evidence sets
items.blurb: More than one set of records that can support an answer, once cqa can declare them; any one set satisfies the anchors.

items.title: Baseline traversal through panschema
items.blurb: The baseline looks up neighboring records with panschema's subgraph search instead of its own SPARQL queries.

items.title: Judging the answer
items.blurb: The second tier: the prose answer judged against ground_truth, behind a flag and out of CI.

items.title: Scores across a benchmark
items.blurb: Mean recall and precision over every question, so a retriever's progress shows as one number per run.

items.title: Ranked retrieval
items.blurb: A trace that orders what it retrieved, for measures like MRR and nDCG that reward putting the anchors first. A trace is a set today, so this changes the format.
